adapter_obligations: Only original request epochs and original packet identities may authorize event delivery or deferred responses; TinyUSB events alone contain no generation ticket.
Fence receive immediately on admitted reset/current transport failure. Keep receive, output, bulk-IN/toggle/stall-reset and EP0 ownership acknowledgements distinct.
Capture the document generation when each packet is submitted; reset status submission occurs after document restart and must not reuse the old reset ticket generation.
Retire class response storage only after its exact transport ownership and queued callbacks are settled. Stalling or a protocol failure is not quiescence.
A newer SETUP suppresses an older deferred class reply while preserving the document stop fence. Never submit an old response through TinyUSB current-request state.

Every nonzero configuration selection, including the current value, must fence and settle original endpoint owners before core close/reset/open. Automatic status permission requires supplied affected-endpoint defaults, toggle and halt reset; a retained software halt is not success.
patch_manifest.apply: Apply with patch -p1 to a disposable copy of the exact pinned source, then verify every resulting SHA256 below. Keep vendor originals unchanged.
patch_manifest.license: MIT; preserve the upstream source copyright and permission notices.

rationale.reason: Device state is logical fields rather than a raw compiler-dependent bitfield byte. Both two-byte status responses explicitly serialize little-endian USB wire values. No adapter-side byte normalization is used.

rationale.change: Optional private application CLASS route selector
rationale.reason: The reusable application adapter may choose the configured printer interface for GET_DEVICE_ID high-byte interface encoding and legacy 0x23 SOFT_RESET. Core retains the original request, checks configuration/interface mapping, invokes once, and treats claimed rejection as final. This patch itself contains no printer-specific matcher or duplicated request parser.

Any non-success current EP0 completion latches failure before byte accounting, copies, DATA/ACK callbacks or the DCD successful-status hook. Both directions are stalled; later completion/public transfer calls remain blocked until a new SETUP or real stack reset. Neither the latch nor DCD stall proves controller ownership or queued events are settled.

rationale.change: Preserve bus and in-flight SET_CONFIGURATION context
rationale.reason: configuration_reset clears the whole device object. Save and restore connected/addressed, speed and the current control context when reinitializing a nonzero configuration, so bus connection/address and the actual request/failure state survive. Actual bus reset continues to clear this state through its unchanged path.

USB 2.0 sections 9.1.1.5 and 9.4.5 require affected endpoint defaults, DATA0 toggle and halt reset even when selecting the current configuration. Reenter the existing close/reset/open path for every nonzero selection; repeated zero remains unchanged. DCD endpoint operations must truthfully supply physical programming/defaults and settlement; this core patch does not establish controller quiescence or wire acknowledgment.

patch_manifest.validation_scope: Proposed source bytes and patch/result hashes regenerated from preserved upstream and disposable edited bytes. Existing prepare-script provenance, fuzz-zero application and full effective-source gates are unchanged. No compilation, fixture execution, QEMU, USB transfer, controller port or hardware validation is claimed for this revision.

limits: No controller/MMIO/IRQ/cache/DMA implementation, USB traffic, firmware upload or physical printing. These 20 focused profiles are separate from the ordinary 132-case adapter baseline and continuous-document validation. Recovery documents here use the existing explicit stream-close path. Faults never establish settlement or class reset promises.
scope: Exact-cookie retained packet faults through the reusable adapter and patched pinned TinyUSB, with independent wire/pixel oracles and supplied ownership settlement.

audit.scope: All annotated code uses the conservative standard ISA; unused encoder code remains. Not a device instruction trace.
